minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard Monty Tech and Sewer Commission FY20 budgets; sewer rate held flat, Monty Tech's Lunenburg share falls.
minutes.summary: A resident who sits on another board criticised the budget process, saying the Board of Selectmen had not discussed the town manager's preliminary budget before the Finance Committee saw it. Monty Tech presented its proposed FY20 budget and Lunenburg's assessment, and the Sewer Commission presented a balanced enterprise-fund budget with no rate increase. The town manager gave updated revenue and expense figures, and the committee approved the February 14 minutes before adjourning.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the Monty Tech FY20 budget, which raises total member assessments while Lunenburg's proposed assessment falls on lower enrollment.
The Sewer Commission presented a balanced FY20 enterprise-fund budget with the sewer rate held flat and Fitchburg's charge rising.
The town manager reported lower overall expenditures, from lower health insurance, a lower Monty Tech assessment and other adjustments.
Schools and DPW will present at the March 14 meeting; the town manager will meet school leaders to re-examine the school numbers.
A resident said Selectmen had not discussed the preliminary budget before the Finance Committee saw it, and suggested a joint workshop after Town Meeting.

why_it_matters: Monty Tech's assessment is paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, so a lower Lunenburg share eases pressure on the tax bill even as the school's total budget grows.
Holding the sewer rate flat means no increase for sewer users from this budget, since the sewer fund is paid by its own rates rather than general taxes.
The school and DPW budgets are still to come, and the school numbers are being re-examined, so the overall FY20 picture is not yet settled.
